Level D

Making Things Happen: Item Use

Add conditional logic to make items interactive

What You'll Learn

1 Implement conditional logic for different item behaviours
2 Return descriptive strings based on outcomes
3 Integrate item use with healing
4 Handle edge cases and invalid inputs

Key Terms

Term Definition
Conditional Logic Using if/elif/else to choose between actions
Method Integration Calling other methods from within a method
Consumable An item that is removed from inventory after use
Return Value The string result that describes what happened

New Methods

NEW Methods to add this level

Structure Guide

Click each section to expand. Add new methods to your existing classes.

1 consume (in Inventory)
METHOD consume(item_id) → boolean:
Purpose: Remove a consumable item from inventory

Works the same as remove() — the engine decides what's consumable.
2 use_item Setup (in Player)
METHOD use_item(item_id, target) → string:
First: Check if item is in inventory
If not found, return: "You don't have 'item_id'."
3 use_item Logic
Use conditional logic to handle each item type:
  • keycard → return unlock message
  • crowbar → return pry open message
  • med_patch → call heal(20), consume item, return heal message
  • torch → return illuminate message
  • other → return "not sure how to use" message
4 Method Chaining Example
For med_patch, your code should:
  1. Call heal(20) to increase health
  2. Call inventory.consume("med_patch") to remove it
  3. Return a message like "You apply the med patch. +20 HP"
This is method integration — use_item calls heal and consume.
